landing.tagline: A private journal for gratitude and bright moments.
landing.lead: Each entry is a small light you put into the jar. Notice the good, see who makes it possible, and come back to it on a darker day.

points.quick: Write a bright moment in under 30 seconds.
points.private: Only you can see your entries. The database itself enforces it.

privacy.title: Your privacy
privacy.intro: Jar of Light is a private journal. Here is, in plain words, who can see what and how we protect it.

sections.heading: Only you see your entries
sections.body: Every entry, category and profile setting is tied to your account. The database itself checks every request with row-level security, so another account can't read or change your data, even through a bug in the app.

sections.heading: What we store
sections.body: Your name and email from Google, your interface language and time zone, and the entries and categories you create. We don't store your Google password and never see it. Nothing is published or shared: there are no public features yet.

sections.heading: Who else has technical access
sections.body: The operator of the service (the author of this project) technically has access to the database to keep it running and does not read entries. Entries are encrypted in transit and at rest by our providers, but not end-to-end: end-to-end encryption would make future features such as search and summaries impossible, so we chose strict access rules instead.

sections.heading: Where the data lives
sections.body: The app runs on Vercel, and the database on Supabase in the United States (Ohio). Sign-in uses Google. There is no advertising and no analytics in this version.

sections.heading: Backups
sections.body: To protect your journal from loss, we make nightly encrypted backups and keep each one for 30 days.

sections.heading: Deleting your data
sections.body: You can delete any entry, or your whole account, in the app at any time. Deletion is immediate; copies in encrypted backups disappear within 30 days.

sections.heading: Questions
sections.body: Write to the author through the project's GitHub page.

about.title: About
about.headline: Fill your life with bright memories.
about.intro: Jar of Light helps you build a habit of noticing the good and being grateful for it.
about.story: Every day brings worries and anxieties, and it's easy to start feeling that life is hard, dark and dangerous. But there is another way: each day, write down one bright moment, one thing you're grateful for. A warm meeting, unexpected help, a bright evening with family and loved ones. Entry by entry, you fill your own jar of light with bright memories.
about.why: An action we repeat regularly becomes automatic over time — a habit<ref>1</ref>. Gratitude also changes how the brain works: after a few weeks of gratitude writing, the brain's response to gratitude was stronger even three months later<ref>2</ref>. Studies show that writing down good things raises life satisfaction and helps people feel joy and look to the future with optimism more often<ref>3,4,5</ref>. As you add to your jar every day, you learn to meet life with trust and warmth.
about.outro: And once the jar is full, you can return to it like a personal diary or a treasure chest: read it again and make your day brighter.

sources.text: Lally P., van Jaarsveld C. H. M., Potts H. W. W., Wardle J. (2010). How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world. European Journal of Social Psychology, 40(6), 998–1009.
Kini P., Wong J., McInnis S., Gabana N., Brown J. W. (2016). The effects of gratitude expression on neural activity. NeuroImage, 128, 1–10.

Emmons R. A., McCullough M. E. (2003). Counting blessings versus burdens: An experimental investigation of gratitude and subjective well-being in daily life. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 84(2), 377–389.
